reasons: Directionally correct: HDI is the host/vendor and the Company (our client) is the customer; Section 4.2(a) imposes the Termination Payment on our side only, so the finding protects our party.

Classification is sound. The 90-day mutual notice in Section 4.1 against a one-year auto-renewing term sits at the fallback (60–90 days' notice; effectively end-of-term exit for HDI) and is correctly left unflagged; the material failure is the exit price — 50% of preceding twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, which is uncapped and plainly many multiples of three months' fees (fees being a revenue share). That breaches the fallback's early-termination fee cap, so 'deviation' rather than 'compliant' is right.

Redline is actionable and proportionate: it preserves the original operative sentence and appends a proviso capping the Termination Payment at three months' fees and disapplying it where we terminate for failure to launch or HDI's breach — exactly the 'replace penalties with the fallback fee cap' remedy in the redline guidance, without over-reaching to delete the payment or upgrade the notice period to the preferred 30 days.

Failed deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' is a false negative: Section 4.1 (p0024) already gives either Party a 90-day exit, so no new Customer right needs to be inserted. The 0.902 changed-character ratio reflects an appended proviso to a short clause, not a gratuitous rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, correctly states the arithmetic ('half of a full year's Net Sales above $800,000') and cites the three-months'-fees fallback.

Minor point to verify before sending: the inserted cross-references (fees 'under Section 3.1' and the Section 1.6 launch-failure carve-out) are not in the supplied paragraphs; confirm the section numbers match the executed document, and note clause (ii) may be partly redundant if Section 4.2(b) already excludes a Section 1.6 termination.
